statements.text: Thank you, Chairman Gallagher, for your leadership on this issue and to our witnesses for helping to inform Congress on these important issues. [...] I am concerned with the rapid advances in artificial intelligence and machine learning, specifically with our adversaries like China.
statements.context: House hearing on AI in military applications where Rep. LaLota introduces transparency legislation and questions witnesses on DOD AI adoption relative to adversaries.

statements.text: The integration of AI and machine learning technologies with unmanned and remotely operated undersea vehicles is critical to enabling UUVs to operate independently and autonomously.
statements.context: Written question for the record submitted by Representative LaLota to Admiral Aquilino during a House Armed Services Committee hearing on U.S. military posture in the Indo-Pacific.

statements.text: And any AI used within the House must meet the highest standards for data security and privacy, and I appreciate your commentary earlier. And, most importantly, it must never be used in a way that undermines the trust or safety of Members, staff, or the American people.
statements.context: House Appropriations Subcommittee hearing on Legislative Branch funding for FY2026.

statements.text: You know, artificial intelligence, probably the biggest area where that is assisting us is in the screening process, where you have X-ray machines that can identify prohibited items when they come through. And that technology is improving every single day. And so we certainly stay in touch with the vendor that we use for our machines to make sure that we have the latest upgrades from that vendor. You know, it is not perfect. You are always going to need to have human eyes on those screens and human interactions with those individuals that have been identified as to having some prohibited item. But the AI helps us avoid those what we call single points of failure, where you can have one person miss something and then you could have a problem. AI can give us that backup, which is better for our security campus-wide.
statements.context: U.S. House Legislative Branch Appropriations hearing for fiscal year 2026, discussing the U.S. Capitol Police modernization plan.

statements.text: At a time where a department that is inherently research- and process-based has a new tool in AI to avail itself of, at the same time that you are able to gain those efficiencies, you are also asking for 8 percent—not 2 or 3 percent, but 8—in order to build your staff up. [...] So I guess my question then, Doctor, is: Why does the CBO need more people at a time where there is such a tool out there to make your job more efficient, sir?
statements.context: House Appropriations Subcommittee hearing on the Legislative Branch budget for Fiscal Year 2026, questioning the Congressional Budget Office Director about staffing requests.

statements.text: So I guess my question is, can you show us a report looking internally to your 270-person department that harnesses AI and to tell us that, given AI, you might need less people or you might be able to cut costs or provide more efficiencies?
statements.context: House Legislative Branch Appropriations hearing for FY2026, where a member questions an agency head about using AI to reduce staffing costs.
